h1: Na Rim Khong River View — the Mekong-side boutique where you wake up and open the balcony to the river
intro: If you come to Nong Khai and want to actually sleep on the Mekong — not just "near the river" — Na Rim Khong River View is the name reviewers keep mentioning. It's a small boutique hotel built right on the riverbank next to Tha Sadet Market and the walking street. The selling point is clear: most rooms have a private balcony that opens straight onto the Mekong and the Laos bank across the water. Rooms start at around THB 2,500/night, including a breakfast that many guests say is so big it keeps them full until midday.

body.html: Na Rim Khong River View is a small property set right on the bank of the Mekong in the Tha Sadet Market area, in the heart of Nong Khai town. What sets it apart from other hotels in town is that the building faces directly onto the Mekong, so most rooms come with a private balcony that opens onto the water and the Laos bank on the far side. This isn't a distant "river view" through a window — it's a balcony where you can sip coffee and watch boats drift past, which is the main reason people choose to stay here.

The location is a clear advantage. The hotel sits right next to Tha Sadet Market, the riverside market selling local snacks, souvenirs and goods from Laos, and it's a few minutes' walk to the Nong Khai walking street that opens on weekends. Step outside and you can stroll along the river, catch the sunset, or grab dinner without calling a car. For travellers who come to Nong Khai for the riverside atmosphere and the border-town pace, this beats hotels tucked deeper inside town.
"Woke up, opened the balcony door, and there was mist drifting over the Mekong with fishing boats going by — I had breakfast right there and didn't want to go anywhere all morning."

After the view, the thing guests praise most is the breakfast. Many reviews agree that the breakfast here is generous and filling, with both Thai and Western options, and you can have it served on your riverside balcony — some say one meal kept them going until the afternoon. The rooms are clean and simply styled, with comfortable beds and decent space, plus air-con, TV, fridge and minibar — everything you need to relax. Staff regularly earn compliments for being warm and attentive.

The one thing to understand before booking is parking and access. Because the property sits right on the riverbank inside the market zone, cars can't drive up to the entrance — you park at a lot about 5–10 minutes away and the hotel runs a tuk-tuk shuttle. That's convenient if you call ahead, but anyone expecting to drive straight to the lobby may find it unfamiliar at first. A few reviews also note there are too few power outlets in the rooms, so bring a power strip if you have several devices to charge. And being a small atmosphere-led place, there's no gym or spa here.

Price is another talking point. Rooms start at around THB 2,500–2,800/night, which some reviewers feel is a bit above the going rate in Nong Khai. Most, though, conclude that you're getting a genuine waterfront position, a private balcony and a generous breakfast in return, and that it's worth the experience. Put simply, you pay a little more for a spot on the river that's hard to find elsewhere in this town.

In short, Na Rim Khong River View suits travellers who come to Nong Khai mainly for the Mekong riverside atmosphere — people who want to wake up to the river, wander Tha Sadet Market, and watch the sun set over the water at an easy pace. If you can live with parking away from the building and a property without luxury facilities, this place delivers what many town hotels can't: actually sleeping on the Mekong.

A tip from reading the reviews: when booking, clearly request a room facing the Mekong with a balcony, since the view is the whole point here. Call ahead with your arrival time so the hotel can send the tuk-tuk to collect you from the car park. And keep your evening free to sit on the balcony for the riverside sunset — the prettiest hour of the day.

honestSummary: Na Rim Khong River View is a boutique that sells a genuine spot on the Mekong, a private balcony in every room, and a generous breakfast in the Tha Sadet Market area in the centre of town. It's a strong fit for travellers who come to Nong Khai for the riverside atmosphere. Just be ready for prices above the town average, parking away from the building, and the lack of big-hotel facilities.

faqTitle: FAQ — Na Rim Khong River View, Nong Khai

faq.q: Where is Na Rim Khong River View · is it really on the Mekong?
faq.a: It's at 423 Moo 5, Meechai Road, on the Mekong riverbank in the Tha Sadet Market area of Mueang Nong Khai. The building faces straight onto the Mekong, and most rooms have a private balcony overlooking the river and the Laos bank. It's right next to Tha Sadet Market and within walking distance of the Nong Khai walking street.

faq.q: How much does Na Rim Khong River View cost · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 2,500/night for a single-bed room and about THB 2,800 for a double, both with a Mekong-view balcony. Prices vary by season and promotion, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What is parking like at Na Rim Khong River View?
faq.a: Because the property is inside the riverside market zone, cars can't reach the entrance — you park at a lot about 5–10 minutes away and the hotel runs a tuk-tuk shuttle. Call ahead with your arrival time so they can send a ride.

faq.q: What is the breakfast like at Na Rim Khong River View?
faq.a: Breakfast is included and widely praised — generous, with both Thai and Western options, and many guests say it keeps them full until afternoon. You can have it served on your riverside balcony, and it's the meal most reviews remember best.

faq.q: Who is Na Rim Khong River View best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for travellers who come to Nong Khai for the Mekong riverside, couples, and anyone who wants to genuinely sleep on the water. If you can accept parking away from the building and no gym/spa, it offers a riverside view and location that's hard to find in town.

faq.q: What's near Na Rim Khong River View?
faq.a: It's right next to Tha Sadet Market and a short walk to the weekend walking street. A short drive reaches Luang Pho Phra Sai (Wat Pho Chai) in about 8 minutes, and Sala Kaew Ku and the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge in about 15. It's ideal for riverside strolls and watching the sunset.
